title: Credit for Time-of-Service Payments Against a Non-Covered Insured Plan of Care Visit
content:
What the patient already paid at the time of service for a non-covered Insured Plan of Care visit is credited against the non-covered charge for that visit:

- payments applied to the **copay charge** of that visit are credited in full;
- where no copay was paid for that visit, payments applied to the **deductible estimate** of that visit are credited instead;
- otherwise nothing is credited.

The credit is subtracted from the charge as priced for the visit, after any discount has acted on it, and the charge is never taken below zero.

## Questions and answers

**Which payments count?** Patient payments on the plan that were applied to the copay charge, or to the deductible estimate charge, posted for the same date of service as the charged visit.

**What if the patient paid both a copay and a deductible estimate for that visit?** Only the copay payments are credited.

**What if the payments exceed the priced charge?** The charge is $0.00; it never becomes negative.

## Hypothetical illustrations (charge as priced $90.00)

| Paid for the visit at the time of service | Credited | Charge after credit |
|---|---|---|
| $30.00 applied to the copay charge | $30.00 | $60.00 |
| Nothing on the copay; $50.00 applied to the deductible estimate | $50.00 | $40.00 |
| $30.00 on the copay and $50.00 on the deductible estimate | $30.00 | $60.00 |
| Nothing applied to either | $0.00 | $90.00 |
| $95.00 applied to the copay charge | $95.00 | $0.00 |
